specification.problem: Compute the weighted sum S = sum_j w_j x_j (and, as a variant, the inner product sum_k x_k y_k) into an accumulator register using Draper QFT phase addition, then read the result by inverse QFT and measurement. The weighted average is obtained by classical division by sum_j w_j.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One smallest construction: a classical-weight weighted sum of k=2 unsigned n=2-bit inputs x_1,x_2 with small non-negative integer weights, in an accumulator of m=n+ceil(log2 k)+(weight headroom) qubits, with basis-state inputs. Signed inputs, the quantum-quantum inner product (CCP), the controlled version and the fixed-point average are described but treated as extensions. Not covered: the paper's exact circuit layouts, resource counts and modular-multiplier variants.

symbols.meaning: accumulator qubit count; chosen so that no overflow occurs in non-modular mode
j-th input integer, bits x_{j,i} with i=0 least significant
accumulator computational-basis value, qubit l carries bit l (little-endian)

equations.label: Fourier-basis accumulator state (no swaps)
equations.description: Qubit l carries phase exp(2 pi i a/2^(l+1)) (up to qubit-order convention).
equations.justification: Standard QFT product form, as in the Draper adder; the sketch states this.
assumptions: Little-endian: qubit l has weight 2^l in a

equations.label: Draper addition by controlled phases
equations.description: Controlled phases from each bit x_i onto each accumulator qubit l add x to a in the Fourier domain, modulo 2^m.
equations.abstract_quote: The Quantum Fourier Transform offers an interesting way to perform arithmetic operations on a quantum computer.
equations.justification: The abstract only says QFT arithmetic with adders exists; the exact angles are the standard Draper construction.
assumptions: Angles for angle>=2 pi can be reduced mod 2 pi

equations.label: Weighted-sum phase angles
equations.description: Multiplying each angle by the classical weight w_j accumulates the weighted sum; a negative w_j gives subtraction.
equations.abstract_quote: we discuss a quantum method to compute the weighted average of a series of inputs in the transform domain
equations.justification: The weighted sum in the transform domain follows from phase additivity; the explicit angle schedule is the standard multiply-by-constant extension.
assumptions: Integer weights, so that the angles are exact

equations.label: Inner product via doubly controlled phases
equations.latex: \theta_{i,j,l}=\frac{2\pi\,2^{i+j}}{2^{l+1}}\ \text{(CCP from } x_i,y_j\text{ to qubit }l),\quad a\to a+\sum_k x_k y_k \bmod 2^m
equations.description: Quantum-quantum multiply-accumulate; repeating over vector entries k gives the inner product.
equations.abstract_quote: One of the circuits, the controlled weighted sum, can be interpreted as a circuit to compute the inner product of two data vectors.
equations.justification: The inner-product reading of the controlled weighted sum implies product-of-bits controlled phases; this is the extension variant.
assumptions: Out of scope for the smallest instance

equations.label: Readout and weighted average
equations.description: Inverse QFT then measurement gives S exactly if there is no overflow; the average is computed classically and is exact only as a rational. An integer quotient would be floor or rounded.
equations.justification: Inverse QFT is the exact inverse; the division is classical post-processing.

registers.name: x_j
registers.role: input data, unchanged, used as controls

registers.name: A
registers.role: accumulator, starts |0>, ends holding S mod 2^m

specification.initial_state: A in |0...0>; each x_j in a computational basis state (or superposition); no ancillas.

steps.description: Apply QFT without swaps to A.
For each j, i, l apply CP(theta_{j,i,l}) controlled by x_{j,i} on A qubit l; for signed inputs negate the angle of the MSB (weight -2^(n-1)).
Apply inverse QFT (no swaps) to A and measure only A.
Classically divide S by the sum of weights for the weighted average.

specification.measurement: Measure A (m bits) in the computational basis after inverse QFT. In Qiskit counts keys, the last character is accumulator bit 0 (qubit 0 is the least significant bit).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Read S as an integer from the bitstring; for signed mode, interpret in two's complement mod 2^m. Compute the average S/sum(w_j), exactly or as a rational, noting that floor or fixed-point truncation is approximate.
assumptions: Chosen instance: k=2, n=2, small non-negative weights, unsigned inputs, basis-state inputs.
The QFT swaps are omitted consistently in the QFT and inverse QFT.
missing_information: The paper's exact circuit layouts, gate counts and the fixed-point weighted-average scheme.
How the controlled and signed variants are arranged in the paper.
The qubit cap and the instances are not given.
